overview.short: Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple is an ancient Shiva shrine in Thrikkariyoor near Kothamangalam, Ernakulam district, Kerala. Believed to be the original capital of the Chera kingdom and one of Kerala's 108 Shiva Temples, it features classical Kerala Dravidian architecture.
overview.description: Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple is an ancient, revered Hindu sanctuary located in Thrikkariyoor near Kothamangalam in Ernakulam district, Kerala. Believed to have been the original capital (Karur) of the ancient Chera dynasty and one of the 108 venerated Shiva Temples consecrated by Lord Parashurama, the temple boasts classic Kerala Dravidian architecture with a circular stone sanctum (Vatta Sreekovil), copper-plated conical roof, ornate Namaskara Mandapam, and a sacred temple tank.

topPlaces.name: Thrikkariyoor Heritage Village
topPlaces.distance: 0.5 km from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple, Kerala
topPlaces.description: Thrikkariyoor is an ancient rural settlement associated with early Chera history. The village features traditional Kerala homesteads (tharavads), lush spice plantations, and quiet countryside roads.

image.alt: Lush green countryside and village pathway in Thrikkariyoor

topPlaces.travelTime: ~3 mins walk from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple

topPlaces.name: Bhoothathankettu Dam & Nature Reserve
topPlaces.distance: 11 km from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple, Kerala
topPlaces.description: Bhoothathankettu is a scenic dam and natural reservoir enveloped by dense tropical forests on the Periyar River. According to legend, demons attempted to dam the river here using mammoth boulders.

image.alt: Panoramic view of Bhoothathankettu dam spillways and lush green hills

topPlaces.travelTime: ~18 mins drive from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple

topPlaces.name: Thattekad Bird Sanctuary (Salim Ali Sanctuary)
topPlaces.distance: 13 km from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple, Kerala
topPlaces.description: Described by legendary ornithologist Dr. Salim Ali as the 'richest bird habitat in peninsular India', Thattekad lies along the Periyar River and shelters over 300 rare and endemic bird species in pristine lowland rainforests.

image.alt: Dense riverine rainforest canopy at Thattekad Bird Sanctuary

topPlaces.travelTime: ~20 mins drive from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple

topPlaces.name: Kothamangalam Town & Gateway to High Ranges
topPlaces.distance: 4 km from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple, Kerala
topPlaces.description: Known as the 'Gateway of the High Ranges', Kothamangalam is a lively taluk town situated in the foothills of the Western Ghats, famous for its historic trade routes, academic institutions, and spices.

image.alt: Lush rubber and spice plantations near Kothamangalam

topPlaces.travelTime: ~8 mins drive from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple

topPlaces.name: Marthoma Cheriyapally, Kothamangalam
topPlaces.distance: 4 km from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple, Kerala
topPlaces.description: Founded in 1455 AD, Marthoma Cheriyapally is one of the most famous Jacobite Syrian Christian pilgrimage centers in India, holding the sacred tomb of Saint Baselios Yeldo.

image.alt: Historic ornate church facade and arches in Kothamangalam

topPlaces.travelTime: ~8 mins drive from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple

topPlaces.name: Ayyappanmudi Hill Viewpoint
topPlaces.distance: 9 km from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple, Kerala
topPlaces.description: A monolithic rock outcrop rising high above Kothamangalam, Ayyappanmudi features an ancient hilltop temple and sweeping 360-degree sunset panoramas across the Western Ghats and coconut plains.

image.alt: Monolithic rock formation and sunrise view at Ayyappanmudi

topPlaces.travelTime: ~15 mins drive from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple

topPlaces.name: Kottappady Countryside
topPlaces.distance: 6 km from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple, Kerala
topPlaces.description: A pastoral village nestled between Kothamangalam and the forest ridges, Kottappady offers scenic routes lined with pepper vines, nutmeg groves, and tranquil streams.

image.alt: Scenic rubber plantations and countryside trail in Kottappady

topPlaces.travelTime: ~10 mins drive from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple

topPlaces.name: Periyar River Valley at Neriamangalam
topPlaces.distance: 18 km from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple, Kerala
topPlaces.description: The emerald Periyar River flowing past the historic 1935 arched Neriamangalam Bridge creates a stunning gateway into the misty high ranges of Munnar and Idukki.

image.alt: Emerald waters of Periyar River winding through forest-clad mountains

topPlaces.travelTime: ~25 mins drive from Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple

items.note: Thrikkariyoor is a village located in the Nellikuzhi panchayat of Ernakulam district in the Indian state of Kerala. The Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple is located near the village.
Kottappady is a village in Kothamangalam Taluk in Ernakulam district of Kerala State, India. It belongs to Central Kerala Division.

Kothamangalam ([koːd̪ɐmɐŋgɐlɐm]) is a municipality at the foot of the Western Ghats in the Ernakulam district of Kerala, India. It is located 42 km (26.1 mi) east of the district collectorate in Thrikkakara and about 218 km (135.5 mi) north of the state capital Thiruvananthapuram.

items.note: Martha Mariyam Cathedral or St. Mary's Church is a prominent Valiyapally (Principal Church) of the Syriac Orthodox Church situated in Kothamangalam town in the Ernakulam district of Kerala, India.

Mar Thoma Cheriyapally is a Jacobite Syrian Christian Church Church located in Kothamangalam town of Ernakulam district, Kerala, India. The church is believed to have been established in 1455 by 18 families who separated from Marth Maryam Valiyapally.
Nellikuzhi is a Grama panchayat in Kothamangalam Taluk, Ernakulam district, Kerala, situated on the Aluva-Munnar State Highway. Nellikuzhi is famous for its furniture business.
Venduvazhy is a village in Ernakulam District, Kerala, India. The municipal area is Kothamangalam.
Cheruvattoor is a village in the municipality of Kothamangalam, which is located at the foot of the western Ghats in the Ernakulam district of Kerala, India.
